note: Court orders + named events that bear on Bengaluru's three river systems (Vrishabhavathi, Arkavati, Dakshina Pinakini). Bellandur Lake sits in the Koramangala-Challaghatta valley which discharges into the Dakshina Pinakini; the foam-and-fire chronology is logged against that river. The Forward Foundation v State of Karnataka NGT bench is the most consequential ongoing case. Compile pattern matches river-events-madurai.json.

events.title: Bellandur Lake foam catches fire for the first time
events.summary: The foam on the surface of Bellandur Lake - the city's largest at ~317 hectares, fed by the K&C valley sewerage - caught fire on 16 May 2015. Foam rose past the height of the adjacent four-lane Outer Ring Road. The fire burned for hours and was the first event of its kind anywhere in India. The K&C Valley STP complex (218 + 30 MLD design) was operating well under the actual untreated load (estimated 400-500 MLD reaching the lake on a peak day). The event triggered the Forward Foundation NGT petition the same year.

events.title: Forward Foundation files NGT petition against Karnataka for Bellandur-Varthur encroachments
events.summary: Forward Foundation - a Bengaluru-based environmental trust - petitioned the National Green Tribunal documenting encroachments on the rajakaluves (storm-water drains) feeding Bellandur and Varthur, apartment-block buffer-zone violations, and the inability of the K&C Valley STPs to handle the actual sewage load. The case became Forward Foundation v State of Karnataka and is one of the most cited Indian environmental jurisprudence decisions on urban water-body governance.

events.title: Bellandur foam catches fire again
events.summary: Recurrence of the May 2015 foam-fire pattern. By February 2017 the K&C Valley STPs were still over-loaded relative to the upstream sewage volume; toxic foam drifted onto adjacent streets in shoulder-high heaps.

events.title: BBC ranks Bengaluru #2 after Cape Town among 11 cities most likely to run out of water
events.summary: A BBC feature based on UN projections placed Bengaluru second after Cape Town among 11 global cities likely to face Day Zero. The framing was contested in Karnataka, but the underlying arithmetic - BWSSB's then-1,310 MLD Cauvery WTP capacity against a JICA-projected 2034 demand of 2,608 MLD - held. The listing made Bengaluru's water crisis legible internationally and put pressure on the still-unfinished Cauvery Stage V.

events.title: Bellandur foam fire burns for over 30 hours
events.summary: The most severe of the Bellandur fires. Began 19 Feb 2018 and required Karnataka Fire Services plus Indian Air Force helicopters dropping water to extinguish over 30+ hours. The international press coverage that followed was the immediate catalyst for the NGT's Dec 2018 Rs 500 crore order.

events.title: NGT orders Rs 500 crore for Bellandur revival + 30/50/25m buffer-zone enforcement
events.summary: The NGT bench in Forward Foundation v State of Karnataka directed the state government to set aside Rs 500 crore for Bellandur revival and to enforce buffer zones along the lake's edges and feeding rajakaluves: 75 m initially (later modified to 30 m at the perimeter, 50 m for storm-water drains, 25 m for canals). Widely cited as the first time an NGT bench held that a state's failure to maintain a hydraulic system counted as an environmental violation in itself. Bellandur fires have subsided since 2021; the sewage load has not.

events.title: Bellandur fire recurrence (smaller scale)
events.summary: Smaller-scale recurrence of the foam-fire pattern, three years after the 2018 escalation. No fires recorded at Bellandur since this 2021 event; foam events still recur sporadically when STP overflows coincide with upstream rain.

events.title: IISc Groundwater Outlook of Bengaluru City - 65 BBMP wards named critically over-extracted
actors: Indian Institute of Science (Sekhar Muddu group)
events.summary: The BWSSB-commissioned IISc Groundwater Outlook of Bengaluru City (April 2025) mapped 65 BBMP wards as 'over-exploited' on the CGWB framework - including Hebbal, Yelahanka, KR Puram, Koramangala, Vijayanagar, Kengeri, Nagarbhavi, Chamarajpet. The implication: roughly a third of BBMP wards are operating beyond the safe groundwater extraction limit. Cauvery Stage V was meant to relieve these wards via piped supply; under-delivery (see next event) means many remain on groundwater + tankers.

events.title: Cauvery Stage V commissioned at TK Halli
events.summary: Cauvery Stage V commissioned on 16 October 2024 at TK Halli. Design capacity 775 MLD aimed at covering the 110 newly-merged villages and the eight ULBs that BBMP absorbed in 2007. Total project cost was Rs 4,435 crore for the Stage V WTP plus Rs 1,255 crore for 110-villages sewerage (JICA Phase 3 Table 16.2.1, 2017 prices), 85% JICA loan / 7.5% GoK / 7.5% BWSSB. Per The Ken's May 2026 series, actual delivery as of Feb 2026 had reached approximately 400 MLD - just over half of design - because last-mile distribution in the merged villages remains incomplete.

events.title: Greater Bengaluru Authority replaces BBMP under Karnataka Act 36 of 2025
events.summary: The BBMP was dissolved on 15 May 2025 and replaced by the Greater Bengaluru Authority (GBA), an umbrella body composed of five new City Corporations (Central, East, West, North, South) covering 369 wards. Final delimitation was notified on 19 November 2025; name changes added 1 December 2025. The new geography inherits BWSSB's water arithmetic unchanged: the 65 BBMP wards IISc had flagged as critically over-extracted remain over-extracted under whichever new GBA ward number they now carry.

events.title: BWSSB-SUEZ Indirect Potable Reuse pilot at TG Halli (110 MLD design)
events.summary: The 1933-vintage TG Halli (Tippagondanahalli / Chamaraja Sagara) reservoir on the Arkavati - defunct as a freshwater source for three decades due to upstream sewage contamination - is being repurposed under a BWSSB-SUEZ partnership to receive 110 MLD of tertiary-treated wastewater. After blending and residence time the water becomes raw feed for the upstream Cauvery WTP system. The first surviving piped supply system in Bengaluru (1933) is being reborn as the closing of the city's sewerage loop. India's largest indirect-potable-reuse experiment.

events.title: WELL Labs Bengaluru Urban Water Balance - groundwater extraction 1,392 MLD bottom-up vs BWSSB official 800
events.summary: WELL Labs (founded 2023) published a comprehensive bottom-up urban water balance for Bengaluru in January 2024. The headline number: total groundwater extraction at 1,392 MLD, 592 MLD higher than BWSSB's officially-cited 800 MLD. The divergence reframes the city's water question: BWSSB's official Cauvery + groundwater arithmetic projects supply meeting 2034 demand, but if 1,392 MLD is the true number, the deficit is structural and immediate. The report is the canonical citation for The Ken's 'Bengaluru doesn't have a water problem; it has a governance problem' series.
